name: Chris Shula

views.text: Having coached every level of a defense lets you be a resource to every player on it.
Keep the core principles, but tailor the plan to what the players can execute with confidence.
A rough early stretch is a time to stay composed and keep believing in the group.
Give a young pass rush room to build its own packages once it starts winning.
Do the job as yourself; trying to imitate someone else is where coordinators go wrong.
Listen to the players; their feedback makes the plan better.

signatures: sits in on different position meetings instead of watching from above
talks about trusting his players rather than about his own calls
want: to show he earned the job on his own merits and build a young Rams defense into a lasting strength
fear: that he is seen as the boss's college teammate and a famous grandson rather than a coordinator in his own right
voice: Even, unflappable and collaborative; he speaks in measured terms about trust, adaptability and the players' ideas. He rarely sounds rattled by a bad week and credits the room for improvements. He keeps the focus off himself and his family name.

evidence.summary: Reports his promotion to replace Morris; he joined McVay's staff in 2017 after two years with the Chargers, was McVay's college teammate at Miami (Ohio) 2004-2007, and is Don Shula's grandson and David Shula's son. Background.

Team announcement tracing his Rams roles: linebackers, outside linebackers, defensive backs in 2022, then linebackers and pass-rush coordinator; credits him with Ernest Jones's development. No McVay quote.

He says coaching several position groups lets him be a resource for players, keeps the 3-4 base and principles, calls the plan a work in progress, and wants schemes tailored to what players do well. His words.

Feature on his first year: sits in on many meetings, changes schemes as needed, lets the young pass rush build packages, welcomes player feedback, stayed composed through a rough start; McVay calls him steady and unflinching and players praise his trust. Team site.

evidence.publisher: Sports Illustrated (Rams On SI), Zak Gilbert
evidence.summary: Recounts McVay's talk with Shula after a 1-4 start, which Shula says freed him to make calls without fear; rookies Fiske and Verse then surged. McVay calls him mentally tough. Retold a season later.
